adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Colombia - Wikipedia
adds.summary: Wikipedia's 'LGBTQ rights in Colombia' page states the national framework a visitor stands under in Cundinamarca: since 1993 a person may change the gender marker on their Colombian birth certificate, with current options F, M, NB (no binario) and T (transgénero). On 9 July 2026 outgoing justice minister Jorge Iván Cuervo signed Decree 0732 of 2026, which obliges public notaries to complete the request within five business days, makes the first request (and a simultaneous name change) free of charge, and shields the change history from public disclosure. The Constitutional Court's 4 February 2022 ruling ordered the government to offer the nonbinary ('NB') option to everyone and to ask Congress to amend the relevant laws, and since August 2023 passports issued within Colombia offer three gender options (male, female, X). A 2016 report (Cartografía de derechos trans en Colombia, by OutRight Action International, El Aquelarre Trans and PAIIS) documented notaries refusing to process name changes and recommended ending the psychiatric pathologisation of transgender identity. Gender-marker change is a notarial/bureaucratic process with no surgery or court ruling required and applies equally in Cundinamarca.
